stemMd: During ventricular contraction, why do the atrioventricular valves close?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The atria become connected directly to the lungs.

options.label: B
options.textMd: All cardiac muscle becomes electrically inactive.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Ventricular pressure rises above atrial pressure.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Blood must flow backwards into the atria.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The valves actively pump blood using their own ventricles.

explanationMd: A rising ventricular pressure reverses the pressure gradient across the atrioventricular valves, closing them and preventing regurgitation into the atria. Their directionality follows pressure, not a separate pumping chamber.

distractorRationale.e: Valves respond mainly to pressure differences.
distractorRationale.a: The anatomical connections do not change.
distractorRationale.d: Valve closure prevents that backward flow.
distractorRationale.b: Contraction follows activation, not complete inactivity.
